A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ProJo4D and provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables supporting a reliable comparison. v1 ends after its references; v3 additionally contains Appendices A–D, which were included in the comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, future-state prediction, and physical-parameter estimation experiments on synthetic and real-world data, including Tables 2–4 and optimization diagnostics in Figure 3.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results and expanded experiments, including GSO evaluation, optimization ablations, camera-view sensitivity, and analyses in Appendices A–B.

M1.justification: v1 successively optimizes velocity, velocity plus materials, and finally all parameters, keeping geometry and appearance fixed until Stage 3. v3 instead optimizes geometry and appearance jointly with velocity in Stage 1, then adds material parameters for full joint optimization in Stage 2. This substantially changes the central optimization procedure, as confirmed by Table 1 and the optimization equations.

E1.justification: v3 retains the Spring-Gaus synthetic and real-world datasets and PAC-NeRF materials, while adding GSO evaluation covering 12 object shapes. Table 7 also introduces monocular and two-view reconstruction conditions beyond v1's three-view and ten-view evaluations, expanding the tested observation conditions.

E2.justification: v3 adds MASIV to the Spring-Gaus comparison, Vid2Sim and a constitutive-model-aligned GIC variant to GSO comparisons, and Spring-Gaus to PAC-NeRF elasticity comparisons. It also adds Sequential+ and cyclic controls and broadens full-joint comparisons. Conversely, the retained ten-view evaluation compares against GIC without v1's PAC-NeRF and Spring-Gaus comparator results.

E3.justification: Reported post-initialization training budgets change: Spring-Gaus uses 100/100 iterations instead of 100/100/100, while PAC-NeRF Newtonian training changes from 50/50/300 to 100/250. v3 introduces sequential/cyclic control protocols and GSO comparisons with aligned stress formulations. The original three-camera selection and real-world 14-frame training/6-frame testing split remain.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's limited optimization diagnostics, v3 systematically compares sequential, joint, progressive, and cyclic strategies; tests Stage 1 parameter choices across materials; measures initial-geometry and camera-view sensitivity; and evaluates adaptation to the Spring-Gaus framework. Tables 3 and 6–8, Figure 4, and Appendices A–B substantially strengthen analysis of scheduling, robustness, and applicability.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across PAC-NeRF scenes within material categories. v3 extends that reporting convention to additional comparisons but introduces no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Changed deviation values are result changes rather than changes in statistical practice.

E6.justification: Numerous existing results are replaced: three-view Spring-Gaus ProJo4D mean CD changes from 0.97 to 1.60 and PSNR from 22.77 to 22.30; real-world mean PSNR changes from 36.60 to 38.30. These accompany a revised optimization procedure and are not same-procedure gains or losses. v3 also adds GSO, baseline, and ablation results while removing detailed per-object ten-view results.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds explicit mathematical definitions of the different Kirchhoff stress formulations used by PAC-NeRF/GIC and Vid2Sim/Simplicits, absent from v1. This is a limited formal addition supporting the GSO comparison. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs for progressive optimization.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains progressive optimization for more accurate sparse-view inverse physics without architectural changes. v3 adds explicit claims of computational efficiency and physical interpretability relative to MASIV, and reframes the headline mechanism around physics-guided geometry refinement. The research objective and principal contribution remain recognizable.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies full-joint optimization failure by material complexity and argues that coupled parameters make future-trajectory accuracy more informative than individual parameter errors. It also explains velocity-first scheduling and attributes smaller Spring-Gaus transfer gains to fixed anchor connections and limited spatial flexibility. These substantially extend interpretation; the original simulation-cost and nondifferentiability limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D and Table 9 newly document 40K initialization iterations, the 3K/37K initialization breakdown, batch sizes, comparator configurations, and GSO stress formulations. Conversely, v1's project/demo link and explicit cosine-schedule details are omitted. Documentation expands substantially, although Table 9 specifies 40K GIC appearance-refinement iterations while Appendix C states 30K.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially revised around Vid2Sim, MASIV, Simplicits, and neural constitutive modeling, with a new connection to curriculum learning over parameter space. The dedicated discussion distinguishing inverse estimation from generative dynamics is removed, along with several associated references. This changes research positioning beyond citation-format updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, later introduction, related work, and motivation undergo substantial rewriting, including an explicit contribution list. Separate initialization, full-joint, and progressive-method discussions are reorganized into the revised Section 3. Results gain a dedicated ablation section and appendices, while limitations are consolidated into the conclusion.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn for the revised stages; optimization plots are reorganized and expanded with Figures 4 and 7. Tables are substantially restructured, with new GSO, ablation, and training-configuration displays and a condensed camera-view comparison replacing the detailed dense-view grid. PAC-NeRF qualitative panels change, v1's real-world image comparison disappears, and the document adopts a different publication layout.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's limited direct validation of its optimization rationale through scheduling controls, material-wise Stage 1 ablations, and tests on another framework. New MASIV/Vid2Sim comparisons and GSO material-formulation controls strengthen assessment of competitiveness and applicability. Expanded implementation details also help reproducibility. Reporting weaknesses remain, including swapped introductory parameter-error labels relative to Table 2, conflicting GIC refinement budgets, and removal of real-world qualitative examples. These drawbacks do not outweigh the substantial improvement in support for the central contribution.
